RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Alleging bias based solely on the panel’s gender is unsubstantiated and risks damaging your professional reputation. In education, all-female panels frequently occur by chance or demographic representation and do not constitute evidence of discrimination. 

While unconscious in-group preference is always a slight possibility, principal appointments typically hinge on interview performance, leadership vision, references, and institutional fit—not paper credentials alone. The other candidate's decade of classroom experience may also have aligned with the school's priorities. 

Do not mention the panel’s composition. Instead, follow up professionally on your request for the written explanation to review how candidates were scored against the objective selection criteria.
